docs.title: slim-guard
docs.text:
slim-guard is the official Slim 4 adapter for guard-core-php, the PHP port of the guard-core security engine. It wires the engine into Slim's middleware stack by composing psr15-guard (the PSR-15 middleware adapter for the same engine) and adds only the Slim-specific integration layer: factory wiring, one-call attachment, and middleware ordering guidance.

All security logic lives in the engine; this package contains no security logic and no duplication of the PSR-15 adapter. Every verdict comes from GuardEngine::execute(), and block responses are translated by the composed psr15-guard middleware.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
composer require rennf93/slim-guard

Requires PHP 8.2 or later. Until rennf93/guard-core-php and rennf93/psr15-guard have Packagist distributions, point composer at their repositories and allow dev stability:

{
    "minimum-stability": "dev",
    "prefer-stable": true,
    "repositories": [
        { "type": "vcs", "url": "https://github.com/Guard-Core/guard-core-php" },
        { "type": "vcs", "url": "https://github.com/Guard-Core/psr15-guard" }
    ]
}

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
use RenzoFranceschini\GuardCore\Config\SecurityConfig;
use RenzoFranceschini\GuardCore\Engine\GuardEngine;
use RenzoFranceschini\GuardCoreSlim\SlimGuard;
use Slim\Factory\AppFactory;

$app = AppFactory::create();

SlimGuard::forApp($app, new GuardEngine(new SecurityConfig(
    enableRedis: true,
    redisPrefix: 'guard_core:',
    rateLimit: 100,
    rateLimitWindow: 60,
)))->addTo($app);

Blocked requests get the engine's GuardResponse translated to a PSR-7 response by psr15-guard (status, body, headers). Passing requests continue into Slim's middleware stack untouched.

docs.title: What the wiring layer handles
docs.text:
• Factory wiring: the response factory comes from $app->getResponseFactory(), and a matching stream factory is resolved (explicit argument, response factory that is also a stream factory, or the default slim/psr7 factory)
  • Attachment: app-level (addTo) screens everything that reaches the app, including unmatched routes that would 404; group-level (addToGroup) only screens requests that match a route inside the group
  • Ordering: the last middleware added executes first in Slim; add the guard last so it runs before anything reads the request body stream
  • Statelessness: SlimGuard and the composed middleware hold no mutable state

See Usage for the full adapter surface and Configuration for engine tuning. Runnable apps live in the examples directory.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The adapter has no options of its own; all security tuning is engine configuration via RenzoFranceschini\GuardCore\Config\SecurityConfig. See the guard-core-php source for the full surface.

docs.title: Minimal tuned setup
docs.text:
$config = new SecurityConfig(
    enableRedis: true,
    redisPrefix: 'guard_core:',
    redisFailOpen: true,
    enableRateLimiting: true,
    rateLimit: 30,
    rateLimitWindow: 60,
    endpointRateLimits: [
        '/rate/strict' => ['limit' => 1, 'window' => 10],
    ],
    enableIpBanning: true,
    autoBanThreshold: 5,
    autoBanDuration: 300,
    customErrorResponses: [403 => 'Blocked by slim-guard'],
    excludePaths: ['/health'],
);

Endpoint rate limits are keyed by URL path and override the global limit for those paths. excludePaths matches a path exactly or as a directory prefix.

docs.title: Redis
docs.text:
Distributed bans and rate limits require Redis:

$config = new SecurityConfig(
    enableRedis: true,
    redisPrefix: 'guard_core:',
);

The engine connects to REDIS_HOST (default 127.0.0.1) and REDIS_PORT (default 6379) from the environment. With redisFailOpen: true the middleware constructs and serves requests even when Redis is unreachable; with redisFailOpen: false construction fails closed. Without Redis the managers fall back to in-process state, which does not share across replicas.

docs.title: Excluded detection headers
docs.text:
The engine skips the ssrf category for the proxy identity headers (host, x-forwarded-for, x-real-ip, cf-connecting-ip, forwarded, ...) by default, so a benign Host header such as localhost:8080 does not trigger a block with every detection category enabled. Every other category (sqli, xss, cmd_injection, and so on) still scans those headers.

Pass excludedDetectionHeaders to extend that set with your own address-carrying headers, and excludedSemanticDetectionHeaders to keep a header (for example a JWT session cookie) out of the semantic analyzer only:

$config = new SecurityConfig(
    excludedDetectionHeaders: ['x-custom-proxy-ip'],
    excludedSemanticDetectionHeaders: ['x-session-token'],
    // ...
);

Do not disable the ssrf category to work around address headers, and do not try to mutate the request inside the middleware, the adapter does not support it.

docs.title: Body inspection
docs.text: PsrGuardRequest::MAX_BODY_BYTES (256 KiB, matching the engine's full-scan window) bounds what the detector sees. Bodies larger than the limit are still forwarded to your handler; only the inspected prefix is truncated, and signatures split across the boundary are not detected. The bound is deliberate and engine-coupled; do not widen it in consumer code.

docs.title: Trusted proxies
docs.text:
When behind a reverse proxy, trust only the proxy hop so the engine resolves the real client IP from forwarded headers:

$config = new SecurityConfig(
    trustedProxies: ['172.16.0.0/12', '10.0.0.0/8'],
    trustedProxyDepth: 1,
    // ...
);

docs.title: Pending-psr15-release: pass-through parity surface
docs.text: Slim composes the psr15-guard middleware, so the pass-through parity surface (engine security headers and CORS verdict headers applied to the handler response, behavioral return rules over a bounded response-body prefix, per-route RouteConfig attachment through a routes map or resolver, and the geo rate-limit resolver) arrives with the psr15-guard release at the 4.2.0 train; until then slim's runtime stays on the released 1.x API. CI mounts the psr15-guard master sibling and bin/test_slim.php exercises the surface there, skipping with an explicit message over the released resolution.

docs.title: Construction
docs.text:
final class SlimGuard
{
    public function __construct(
        ResponseFactoryInterface $responseFactory,
        StreamFactoryInterface $streamFactory,
        GuardEngine $engine,
        ?SecurityDecorator $decoratorHandler = null,
        ?object $agentHandler = null
    ) { ... }

    public static function forApp(
        App $app,
        GuardEngine $engine,
        ?StreamFactoryInterface $streamFactory = null,
        ?object $agentHandler = null,
        ?SecurityDecorator $decoratorHandler = null
    ): self;
    public function middleware(): MiddlewareInterface;
    public function addTo(App $app): App;
    public function addToGroup(RouteGroupInterface $group): RouteGroupInterface;
    public function statusRoute(App $app, string $path = '/_guard/status'): void;
    public function agentStats(): array;
    public function reset(): void;
    public function refreshCloudIpRanges(): void;
}

SlimGuard::forApp() builds the guard from an existing Slim App: the response factory is the app's own, and the stream factory resolves from the explicit argument, then a response factory that also implements StreamFactoryInterface, then the default slim/psr7 factory when installed. A LogicException is thrown when none of those apply; pass a StreamFactoryInterface explicitly instead of relying on slim/psr7.

The constructor composes the psr15-guard GuardMiddleware, which calls $engine->initialize(); a GuardRedisException is swallowed only when SecurityConfig.redisFailOpen is true, otherwise construction fails closed.

docs.title: Attachment
docs.text:
SlimGuard::forApp($app, $engine)->addTo($app);        // app middleware: screens everything, including 404s

$group = $app->group('/admin', function ($group) { ... });
SlimGuard::forApp($groupApp, $adminEngine)->addToGroup($group);
                                                       // group middleware: only screens matched routes

middleware() exposes the composed PSR-15 middleware for hand wiring ($app->add($slimGuard->middleware())) or for any stack that accepts PSR-15 middleware.

docs.title: Middleware ordering
docs.text: Slim runs the last-added middleware first. Add the guard AFTER (in code order) any middleware that reads the request body stream: Slim's optional BodyParsingMiddleware casts the stream to a string, which leaves the read pointer at EOF and starves the engine's bounded body scan. The guard should be added last so it executes first.

docs.title: Verdicts
docs.text:
Block verdicts are translated by the composed psr15-guard middleware and never reach your route callable:

Situation Status Body Banned IP 403 IP address banned Suspicious content 400 Suspicious activity detected Rate limit exceeded 429 Too many requests plus Retry-After Engine malfunction 500 Security check failed

Bodies can be overridden globally through SecurityConfig.customErrorResponses.

docs.title: Telemetry agent and dynamic rules
docs.text:
The adapter forwards an optional agentHandler to the engine (GuardEngine::setAgentHandler()), so security events, metrics and dashboard dynamic rules flow through guard-agent-php. Install it with composer require rennf93/guard-agent-php, create and start the agent where the Slim App is assembled, pass it as the agentHandler argument, and declare it in the config with enableAgent: true:

use RenzoFranceschini\GuardAgent\GuardAgent;
use RenzoFranceschini\GuardCore\Config\SecurityConfig;
use RenzoFranceschini\GuardCore\Engine\GuardEngine;

$agent = new GuardAgent([
    'apiKey' => $_ENV['GUARD_API_KEY'],
    'endpoint' => 'https://api.guard-core.com',
    'projectId' => 'my-project',
]);
$agent->start();

$config = new SecurityConfig(
    enableRedis: true,
    enableAgent: true,
    enableDynamicRules: true,
    dynamicRuleInterval: 300,
    enableEnrichment: true,
    agentProjectId: 'my-project',
);

SlimGuard::forApp($app, new GuardEngine($config), agentHandler: $agent)->addTo($app);

// or with the plain constructor
$guard = new SlimGuard($app->getResponseFactory(), $streamFactory, new GuardEngine($config), agentHandler: $agent);

register_shutdown_function(static function () use ($agent): void {
    $agent->flushBuffer();
    $agent->stop();
});

enableDynamicRules and enableEnrichment require enableAgent, and dynamic rules need an agent handler that exposes getDynamicRules() (GuardAgent does). The engine builds the dynamic rule manager itself and checks for new rules on the first request and then every dynamicRuleInterval seconds (default 300, minimum 60), because a PHP request process has no background loop. Without an agent handler the engine warns and stays on the static config. agentStats() on the adapter reports {enabled: false, degraded: false} without a handler and merges the handler's getStats() map with one.

docs.title: Response modifier
docs.text:
SecurityConfig::customResponseModifier is a Closure(GuardResponse): GuardResponse that the engine applies once to every response it returns itself (blocks, redirects and the fail-closed response), after the security headers and before the CORS verdict headers. This adapter applies the same modifier to the pass-through responses it sends, through GuardEngine::applyResponseModifier(), including excluded-path responses and responses of requests that bypass all checks, and it never applies it twice to a response the engine already modified. The order on a pass-through response is security headers, modifier, then CORS verdict headers, so the CORS policy has the last word on its own headers.

use RenzoFranceschini\GuardCore\Request\GuardResponse;

$config = new SecurityConfig(
    customResponseModifier: static function (GuardResponse $response): GuardResponse {
        $response->headers()->set('X-Served-By', 'edge-1');

        return $response;
    },
);

The modifier sees the status, the headers (Set-Cookie is not exposed) and the body, and the changes are merged back onto the PSR-7 response; a response whose body stream is not seekable keeps its body (only its status and headers can change). A modifier that throws leaves the response unmodified. Nothing is read from the response while no modifier is configured. The modifier seam needs guard-core-php 4.4.0 or later.

docs.title: Fail-closed behavior
docs.text: Inherited from psr15-guard: if the engine check throws, the middleware responds with the engine's fail-closed response (500 Security check failed) rather than letting the request through. A custom 500 body comes from customErrorResponses[500], not from adapter code.

docs.title: Route-scoped configuration
docs.text: The engine supports per-route RouteConfig (required headers, per-route rate limits) keyed off a route ID on the request state, and the composed adapter builds its engine request internally, so there is no route-ID hook. The engine-sanctioned equivalent is the customRequestCheck config closure, which runs as the last pipeline check; for Slim-native route scoping, attach a dedicated guard to a route group with addToGroup() and its own engine instance. See the advanced example app.
